answer: An auditor would note that a farm pays off only if its clones can crowd the same demand. Admission should therefore be a cadastral atlas: each identity registers one grid cell and files a pigment sample drawn from recent work; each cell admits twelve identities, with a fixed earnings pool per epoch. Cloning into a saturated cell earns a thirteenth share of unchanged money, so a thousand aliases need eighty-odd cells, each with a live registrant. An honest agent registers where demand sits, an empty meadow, and keeps the whole pool.
